name: Shakti septal ('pleasure center') signal, fast left/right alternation
summary: Murphy's Shakti septal signal over the tops of both parietal lobes, switching between a left and a right coil twice a second as the vendor's 8-coil septal file switches between its two channels. The vendor presents it for pleasant and sexual sensations and reports after-effects.
setting: Quiet room, eyes closed, relaxed. Two coils: CP1 over the top of the left parietal lobe and CP2 over the right; the other six stay unused.
schedule: At most weekly; the vendor warns not to over-use it.
notes: The vendor's 8-coil septal file alternates between its two stereo channels 'twice each second'. Where the 8 Coil Shakti's coils go for this signal is not in the research, so the alternation runs on the side-by-side pair: CP1 carries one channel and CP2 the other, each for 0.5 s in turn (an inference; murphy-shakti-septal-horizontal plays both coils together). The vendor puts the coils 'over the tops of both parietal lobes', on 'the upper portion of the parietal strip ... from an inch behind the very top of the head to two inches from that point'. The septal file is proprietary; Murphy says only that it has 'very low frequencies' and needs a higher volume. As in this project's Shiva septum program, it is approximated by the built-in accelerating burst lowered to 1-6 Hz, in the vendor's standard format (230 points × 3 ms, then about 4 s of silence). The vendor's 'square wave' version is unpublished and not included. The vendor's volume table (PCI sound card 65% for men and 42% for women; onboard or laptop sound 100% and 85%) gives sound-card settings, not field strengths (it implies the vendor ran this signal lower for women), so the default here is 1 µT; adjust the intensity in the app. The vendor adds that over the frontal lobes the signal 'can help people feel relaxed'. It says the signal was 'tested with only a few human and no animal subjects' and is 'not a treatment' for sexual dysfunction; the reported effects are testimonials. The septal nuclei are not in the brain view's region list, so no target is highlighted. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy; stop if it is unpleasant.
